Remark
[The ball $B(y,r_y)$ has compact closure in the cap] ↗ def:c-epsilon-cap

If $B(y,r_y)$ meets the complement of the core, curvature control on the neck bounds $r_y$ by a fixed multiple of the neck curvature scale. Since $\epsilon <1/2$ and $y$ lies in the core, this implies $B(y,r_y)\Subset \mathcal C$. The neck orientation is chosen so that the closure of its negative end meets the core.

\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Condition (8) is a time-derivative bound]
